name: Northwind Retail
summary: A smaller, single-headquarters retailer with an in-store payment network and an e-commerce DMZ. It shows the minimum a valid submission needs: one branch, real segmentation (card data kept apart for PCI), a priced product comparison, and a rule set you can explain line by line.

vlans.name: pos
vlans.note: Point-of-sale terminals; cardholder-data segment, kept apart for PCI-DSS.

vlans.name: iot
vlans.note: Cameras, sensors, digital signage — untrusted, egress-limited.

chosen.reason: Comfortable over the 300 Mbps link, open and auditable for PCI evidence, low cost for a lean retailer.

alternatives.reason: Great UTM; licence recurring, overkill for this size.
Cheapest, nice UI; policy depth too shallow for PCI segmentation.
Good reporting; another licence to carry.

rules.note: Public HTTPS to the storefront in the DMZ.
Rate-limit to absorb bursts and simple floods.
POS talks only to the acquirer's gateway — one destination, nothing else.
Cardholder segment is isolated from the office network (PCI-DSS segmentation).
IoT can never reach the payment segment.
NTP — PCI logs need accurate timestamps.

remoteAccess.note: Store managers get a VPN profile scoped to the back-office app only; the POS vendor gets a separate, time-boxed profile for maintenance windows. No standing public remote access.

monitoring.owner: Outsourced MSSP watches 24/7; the IT lead is the named owner for escalations.
monitoring.alertSink: MSSP portal; Telegram for POS-segment blocks (highest priority).
monitoring.appVsSecurity: Store-uptime alerts go to the ops group; anything touching the POS/cardholder segment is a security event and pages the on-call.
